claims.behaviour: Web-resource `filtersync-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget`. The `sync-filter` form requires it when rendered and starts its behaviour as soon as the form is on the page; loading the resource alone does nothing except fetch the JQL search data (see the next claims).

On the `sync-filter` form the filter choice has two radio buttons. With `savedFilter` chosen the saved-filter area shows and the JQL area hides; with `jql` chosen the JQL area shows and the saved-filter area hides; with neither chosen both are hidden. The switch happens at once on change, and the state is applied on page load from the rendered selection.

On load the `sync-filter` form starts fetching Jira's JQL autocomplete data once. The first time the JQL area is shown, once that fetch has finished (success or failure), autocomplete with live validation is attached to the JQL text area, its status shown beside the field. Later the same instance is only re-enabled. Each time the area shows the text area gets focus. Switching to the saved filter disables autocomplete.

Clicking Select on the `sync-filter` form opens Jira's own filter picker in a popup window named `filter_sf_window`, 800 by 500, resizable with scrollbars, at `/secure/FilterPickerPopup.jspa?showProjects=false&field=sf` (context path prepended), and focuses it; the link itself does not navigate. For the picker to report back, the form exposes the elements Jira's popup looks for with field `sf`: `filter_sf_id` on the hidden `filterid` input, `filter_sf_name_h` on the hidden `filtername` input and `filter_sf_name` on the visible name.

When the `sync-filter` form is submitted with a picked saved filter id, the visible filter name is copied into the hidden `filtername` field first, so that a form redisplayed after a validation error still shows the name. With no id nothing is copied.

Dependent controls of the `sync-filter` form enable and disable live, and disabled ones are not submitted: unchecking Add disables both placement radios; the parent issue key input and the Allow move checkbox are enabled only when Add is checked and the placement is `under`; unchecking Remove disables its two sub-options (`removeWhereAdd`, `forceReCheck`).

The `sync-filter` form's first field is labelled `Filter`, with radios `Saved filter` (`filtertype=savedFilter`) and `JQL query` (`filtertype=jql`). The saved-filter part has hidden `filterid` and `filtername`, then the filter's name when one is known, styled as a success value, or `No filter selected`, then a `Select` link. The JQL part is a 2-row, 45-column text area `filterjql`. Field errors for `filterid` and `filterjql` show under their parts.

The `sync-filter` form's field `Add` has checkbox `add` with text `If an issue passes the filter, add it to the structure.`; radios `addWhere`: `root` `Place added issue at the top level` (selected unless the value is `under`) and `under` `Place added issue as a sub-issue of` followed by a 10-wide text input `addUnder` whose tooltip is `Please enter issue key of the parent issue.`; and nested under them checkbox `addMoveForced`: `Allow move: if the matching issue is already in the structure, but it's not under this "parent" issue, move it.` The `addUnder` error shows under the radio.

The `sync-filter` form's field `Remove` has checkbox `remove` with text `Remove from structure issues that don't pass the filter.` and sub-options `removeWhereAdd` `Remove only from where added issues are placed` and `forceReCheck` `Double-check sub-issues when parent issue no longer passes the filter`. The error under key `remove` shows at the end of this field.
Web-resource `ghsync-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util`. The `sync-gh` form requires it when rendered and starts its behaviour once the form is on the page.

On the `sync-gh` form choosing mode `rapidview` shows the board part and hides the projects part; any other mode, including no mode radios at all (boards not supported), shows the projects part and hides the board part. The ranking options (description, Independent and Consecutive radios, explanation) are one block that moves between the two parts, so there is one set of them in the form.

On the `sync-gh` form the multi-select of projects is initialised on load from the hidden comma-separated `projects` value, and on each change the selected ids are written back to it joined with `,`. Only `projects` carries the selection to the server.

When no project is eligible on the `sync-gh` form the project controls are not rendered, and the form's script stops with an error at the project step, so the ranking block is never enabled or disabled by the rules of the next claim (as the original does).

The ranking options of the `sync-gh` form are enabled when, in board mode, `Synchronize Rank` is checked, and in projects mode when a rank field is selected (non-empty); otherwise their inputs are disabled, hence not submitted, and the description is shown as disabled. The rule follows live, and survives the rank field select being rebuilt when the project selection changes.

The `sync-gh` form starts with the Source of Truth field and, under it, its description `Directs the resolution of conflicts between changes. A conflict is always resolved in favor of either Structure or Jira. Also defines the resync direction.` Then, only when boards can be used, field `Use` with radios `mode`: `rapidview` `Agile Board configuration` and `classic` `Custom projects and fields`, `classic` selected when there is no `viewId` or the mode is `classic`.

The board part of the `sync-gh` form has select `viewId` labelled `Agile Board` listing the boards the user sees by name; a stored id not among them adds a selected option `?`. Then checkbox `syncRank` `Synchronize Rank` and the ranking block: description `Rank will only be synchronized if Ranking is configured for Agile Board.`, radios `independentRanking` `true` `Independent ranking: rank parent issues separately from their sub-issues` and `false` `Consecutive ranking: rank all issues in the order they appear in structure`, the latter selected when the value is not true, and a note saying consecutive ranking is what older versions used. A `viewId` error shows under the select.

On the `sync-gh` form the `Synchronize Rank` checkbox is rendered disabled whenever the epic service is unavailable, so with Jira Software's epic service absent rank cannot be chosen, although rank does not depend on epics (as the original does).

The projects part of the `sync-gh` form has field `Projects`: a multi-select of eligible projects by name, with hidden `projects`, or, with none eligible, the text `No projects suitable for synchronization available`. Then select `rankField` labelled `Rank field`: first option value empty `Don't synchronize`, then each rank custom field as `<name> [<field id>]`; a stored value not listed adds a selected option `?`, which stays through option rebuilding. The options are limited to fields applicable to the selected projects (the shared cascading select). Errors for `project` and `rankField` show under their fields.

The `sync-gh` form ends with, only when the epic service is available, checkbox `syncEpics` `Synchronize Epics` with the description `Jira Software (Jira Agile 6.1+) Epics will be used for synchronization.` and any `syncEpics` error; and always checkbox `subtasks` `Auto-add sub-tasks` with a sentence saying sub-tasks are added under their parent, like the sub-tasks synchronizer.

The shared Source of Truth field, on the `sync-gh` and `sync-links` forms, is labelled `Source of Truth` with radios `sourceOfTruth`: `jira` `Jira`, selected unless the value is `structure`, and `structure` `Structure`. An error under `sourceOfTruth` shows below them.

Web-resource `linksync-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget`. The `sync-links` form requires it, and loading it starts fetching Jira's JQL search data once.

On the `sync-links` form the two options of the `direction` select take their text from the chosen link type: `out` shows its outward description, `in` its inward one, `?` when the chosen option has none (an unknown stored type). This runs on load and on each change of the link type.
On the `sync-links` form the checkboxes `expandchild` and `expandparent` are disabled while `useall` is `true` and enabled otherwise, live and on load.

On the `sync-links` form the description under the primacy checkbox follows the Source of Truth: with `structure` it reads `Structure primacy: Reverse issue link creation/deletion if it contradicts structure`, otherwise `Links primacy: Reverse structure change if it contradicts issue links`.

The `sync-links` form has two filters, parent and child, each with the behaviour of the `sync-filter` form's filter choice with these differences: a third radio `none` hides both areas and disables autocomplete; the picker opens with field `parentsf` or `childsf`, in window `filter_parentsf_window` or `filter_childsf_window`, same size and URL pattern; the elements for Jira's popup are `filter_<field>_id`, `filter_<field>_name_h` and `filter_<field>_name`; each JQL area has its own autocomplete.

When the `sync-links` form is submitted, each filter with a picked id copies its visible name into hidden `parentfiltername` or `childfiltername`. This is attached through the link type select, so with no link types available it does not happen.

The `sync-links` form has the inputs on the left and a help text beside each on the right, in sections: `1. Select Source of Truth and Primacy`, `2. Select Link Type and Direction`, `3. Issue Filters (Optional)`, with a line saying that several links synchronizers on one structure should each have a limited scope to avoid conflicts, and `4. Adjust Advanced Options (Optional)`, with a line saying these give more control but need understanding.

Help texts of the `sync-links` form, each a paragraph or a few, naming the field in bold: Source of Truth (how conflicts resolve, resync direction, which contradicting changes are reverted with primacy); Primacy, 4 or 5 paragraphs (what incremental sync does with primacy off, Structure primacy, Links primacy, no effect during Import, Export and Resync); Link Type (one sentence); Link Direction (one sentence); both filters together, 4 paragraphs (what is not touched, and a warning against filters on conditions that change without the issue changing); Scope (Expand options, and a warning that Synchronize all can delete all links of the type on Export or Resync to links); Removal (Move Upwards versus Remove).
Field `Primacy` of the `sync-links` form is checkbox `useprimacy` `Reverse contradicting changes during Incremental Sync`.

Field `Link Type` of the `sync-links` form is select `linktype` of link types by name, followed by, when hidden types exist, a group `Hidden Types` of them; each option carries its outward and inward descriptions. A stored id not found adds a selected option `?`. With no link types: the text `No link types available` in place of the select.
Field `Link Direction` of the `sync-links` form reads as a sentence: `parent issue`, select `direction` with options `out` and `in`, `sub-issue`. A `direction` error shows under it.

Fields `Parent Issue Filter` and `Sub-Issue Filter` of the `sync-links` form have radios `parentfilter` / `childfilter`: `none` `Not set (all issues allowed)`, `savedFilter` `Saved filter` with hidden `<prefix>filterid`, `<prefix>filtername`, the name or `No filter selected` and link `Select`, and `jql` `JQL query` with 2-row 45-column text area `<prefix>filterjql`. Errors for the id and JQL fields show under their parts.

Radio `none` of the `sync-links` filters is selected only when the field has no value, so when the form comes back after an error with `parentfilter=none` or `childfilter=none`, no radio of that filter is selected; submitting that way still means no filter (as the original does).

Field `Scope` of the `sync-links` form has radios `useall`: `false` `Synchronize issues that are already in the structure`, selected unless `useall` is true, with sub-options `expandchild` `Expand to sub-issues: also include issues with incoming links from other synchronized issues` and `expandparent` `Expand to parent issues: also include issues with outgoing links to other synchronized issues`, and `true` `Synchronize all issues that have links of selected type`.

Field `Removal` of the `sync-links` form has radios `orphanaction`: `move-up` `Move a sub-issue without incoming link upwards in the hierarchy`, selected unless the value is `remove`, and `remove` `Remove sub-issues without incoming link`.

Web-resource `statusup-config-js` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:jquery-ui` (drag-and-drop ordering) and `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` (the checkbox multi-selector, see `page-util`). The `sync-status-rollup` form requires it.

On load the `sync-status-rollup` form sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects` with no parameters and lists the reply's `projects`, each a checkbox by `name` with value `id` and tooltip `description`, plus `All projects enabled for <product>` (value `*`). The selection goes to hidden field `projects`.

On load and whenever the project selection changes, the `sync-status-rollup` form sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/types?projects=<value>`, the hidden field's value URL-encoded (`*` or ids joined with `,`), and lists the reply's `constants`, plus `All types` (value `*`), into hidden `types`.

On load and whenever projects or types change, the `sync-status-rollup` form sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses?projects=<value>&types=<value>`, both URL-encoded, and lists the reply's `constants` with no All option. Each status shows its icon at 16 by 16 before the name when `iconUrl` is set and not `/`, with tooltip `<name> - <description>` when there is a description.

Statuses selected on the `sync-status-rollup` form also appear in a separate ordered list, where they are reordered by drag and drop; the hint `Use drag-and-drop to specify status order:` shows only while the list has entries. Hidden `statuses` holds the ids in that order, comma-joined. A newly checked status goes before the next checked one in the option order, or at the end.

For each selected status known from the loaded options the `sync-status-rollup` form shows one transitions block, in status order, headed by the status (icon, name, tooltip), with a checkbox list that includes `Any possible` (value `*`). When no block exists the text `None` shows instead. Unchecking a status removes its block; a reordering moves blocks without reloading them.

Each transitions block sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitions?projects=<value>&types=<value>&status=<status id>`, URL-encoded, when it is created and again on every change of projects or types. It lists the reply's `transitions`. An option's value is `<URL-encoded workflow>:<action>`; entries without workflow or action are skipped. The label is `<name> (from <source A>, <source B> - <workflow>)`, or `<name> (<workflow>)` without source statuses. The word `from` is the text `from`.

Each status's transition selection is sent in hidden field `transitions-<status id>`, pre-filled from the stored values or created empty for a new status. These fields stay when a status is unchecked, so re-checking the status in the same page visit brings back its earlier value.

All selectors of the `sync-status-rollup` form follow the checkbox multi-selector of `page-util`: `All` checked means value `*` and checks every option; unchecking any option clears `All`; `Loading...` shows after 300 ms of waiting; an older answer is ignored; an empty list shows `None`; a failed load marks the selector as failed. On submit, ids no longer among the loaded options are dropped from the field, unless the value is `*`, so submitting before a list has loaded empties that field.

The `sync-status-rollup` form has, with help beside each field: hidden `projects` with label `Enabled projects`; hidden `types`, `Enabled issue types`; hidden `statuses`, `Statuses rolled up`; `Allowed transitions`; and select `resolution` labelled `Resolution`. Errors under `projects`, `types`, `statuses`, `transitions` and `resolution` show in their fields.

Select `resolution` of the `sync-status-rollup` form has first option, value empty, `Use current or default value`, then Jira's resolutions by localized name. A stored value not found adds a selected option `?`.

Help of the `sync-status-rollup` form, to be written in the implementer's own words: Projects and Types, one or two sentences each, say the parent issue must match and sub-issues need not; Statuses, 4 short paragraphs, explains the earliest-to-latest rule with an example; Transitions, 3 paragraphs, says transitions are tried in order, that with none a status is still counted but not set, and that they run as the installing user and may fail; Resolution, 2 sentences, suggests a dedicated value and says it only applies when the transition allows it.

The `sync-subtasks` form has field `Sub-Task Types`: with no sub-task types the text `No sub-task types are available.`, otherwise the entity selector (`select-entities` claims) on field `types`, offering All and None, with everything selected by default on a new form and the stored value otherwise. An error under `types` shows below it.

The `StructureSync` list page has browser title and page heading `Synchronization Settings - <structure name>` and the current section `wi-structure-link`. Under heading `Automatic Synchronization`, with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window: a warning when one applies (see the page's claims), then a text of about 4 paragraphs saying what synchronization is, that enabled synchronizers apply changes incrementally within seconds or longer, that they can make massive changes with no undo, and to read parameters and back up; then the table.

The `StructureSync` table has columns `Type`, `Description`, `Run as User`, `State` and `Operations`. Description holds the instance description then its detail lines. State holds the state word then, below, one link per line. Operations holds the links separated by ` | `. Without the app permission the Operations cell shows `Restricted`, with no links; for an archived structure with the permission it is empty.

Below the `StructureSync` table, with the permission and not archived, the add form has `Set Up Synchronization With:`, a select of types, the selected type's description beside it updating on change, and button `Configure and Install Synchronizer`. It submits by GET to `StructureSync.jspa` with `id`, `synctype` and `create=true`.

With the app permission the `StructureSync` page has a section `One-Time Synchronization` with two short paragraphs saying Import and Export run the chosen synchronizer once, as Resync would, then links `Import into Structure` (not on an archived structure) and `Export from Structure`. When a return URL is set, a `Back` link closes the page.

The warnings on the `StructureSync` page: without permission, a bold `You currently do not have the permission to manage synchronizers.` and a sentence to ask a Jira administrator; for an archived structure, a bold `This structure is archived.` and sentences saying synchronizers do not work there and to unarchive it first.

The install form of `StructureSync` has title and page heading `Install Synchronizer - <structure name>`, heading `Install Synchronizer : <type label>` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, a note with the type's description and rules, error messages when any, read-only `Structure` and `Run as User`, the synchronizer's form, and buttons `Create` and `Cancel` (a link to the return URL). It posts to `StructureSync!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id`, `create=true`, `execute=true` and `synctype`.

The `Synchronizer Installed` page has title and heading `Synchronizer Installed - <structure name>` and heading `Synchronizer Installed`, then `A new synchronizer has been installed (id <id>).`, two paragraphs saying the synchronizer is `Disabled` and does not track changes, that `Resync and Enable` loses no changes, and that this can be done later; error messages when any; button `Resync and Enable` with `Rescans structure and all relevant issues, synchronize and enable automatic synchronization.`; button `Enable without Resyncing` with `Enable synchronizer without full synchronization`; and `Done`.

The `StructureSyncEdit` form has title `Edit Synchronizer - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `<description> - <structure name>` and heading `Edit Synchronizer`. Below, in order: the success-styled message when the page has just disabled the synchronizer, a note with the synchronizer's description and rules, error messages, read-only `Structure`, the `Run as User` group, the synchronizer's form, and buttons `Apply` and `Cancel`. It posts to `StructureSyncEdit!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `execute=true`, `syncId` and `askOnCancel`.

On the `StructureSyncEdit` form a Jira administrator who is not the owner sees radios `keepOwner`: `true` `Current synchronizer owner — <owner>` and `false` `Current user — <current user>`. `Current user` is selected on first opening, since the `keepOwner` flag is then absent. Anyone else sees the current user as plain text, with `keepOwner=false` sent hidden.

When `StructureSyncEdit` shows errors after validating as the owner (not as the current user), the form ends with `The synchronizer parameters are invalid for user '<owner>'. Please fix the errors above and apply changes again.`

The `StructureSyncEdit` done page has heading `Synchronizer Parameters Updated` with `Synchronizer parameters have been updated.`, or for a cancel `Editing Has Been Cancelled` with `Synchronizer editing has been cancelled.`; browser title `<that heading> - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `<description> - <structure name>`; then the same offer, buttons and explanations as the `Synchronizer Installed` page.

The `StructureSyncDelete` confirmation has browser title `Delete Synchronizer - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `<description> - <structure name>`, heading `Delete Synchronizer`, two sentences saying that it stops and removes the synchronizer, a running synchronization is allowed to finish, and changes already made stay; error messages; read-only `Structure` and `Synchronizer` (description and detail lines); buttons `Delete Synchronizer` and `Cancel`.

The `StructureResync` confirmation has browser title `Resync Now - <description> - <structure name>`, page heading `Resync Now`, heading `Please Confirm Running Full Synchronization` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, 3 paragraphs on resync as a one-time scan in the selected direction versus continuous incremental sync, and its duration; error messages; `Structure`; `Synchronizer`; a hint box `Possible effects during resync:` with a bulleted line per effect; the warning `WARNING: Full synchronization may effect massive changes.`; then, when they apply, a checked and disabled checkbox with the enable notice and the error box on the index. Buttons: `Start Resync`, styled as dangerous, and `Cancel`.

`StructureImport.jspa` without `synctype` has title and page heading `Import Structure - <name, abbreviated to 40 characters>`, heading `Select Import Source` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, `Please select where would you like to import from.`, then `Import From:`, a select with the description beside it and button `Configure Import Parameters`, plus `Cancel`. The export page is the same with `Export Structure - <name>`, `Select Export Target`, `Please select where would you like to export to.`, `Export To:` and `Configure Export Parameters`. With no synchronizers the text is `No import sources available (no synchronizers are capable of importing into structure)` or `No export targets available (no synchronizers are capable of exporting from structure)`. Both submit by GET with `id`.

The import form has title and page heading `Import Parameters - <name, abbreviated to 40 characters>`, heading `Import from <label>` with a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, a note with description and rules, error messages, read-only `Structure` and `Run as User` (the current user), the synchronizer's form, and a warning saying import may completely change the structure, issues are not altered, and a copy makes a backup. Buttons `Run Import` and `Cancel`. It posts to `StructureImport!apply.jspa` with `atl_token`, `id`, `create=true`, `execute=true`, `synctype`. The export form is the same with `Export Parameters - <name>`, `Export to <label>`, a warning saying export may massively change issues, with no Undo, `Run Export` and `StructureExport!apply.jspa`.

Submitting the import or export form first asks in the browser's own confirm box `Run Import?` or `Run Export?`. On Cancel nothing is sent; on OK the submit button is disabled and the form is sent, so a second click cannot send it twice.

Web-resource `effector-common` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:tslib` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:structure-aui`. It provides the status icons and shared styles of effector processes; no behaviour of its own.

Each effector process status has an icon wherever status is shown: pending (never started), calculating, calculated, queued, in progress, completed, failed (`CALCULATION_FAILED`, error icon), stopped (shared by `CALCULATION_STOPPED` and `APPLY_STOPPED`), and completed-with-errors (shared by `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` and `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`).
Web-resource `effector-processes` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util`. The `StructureProcesses` page requires it and starts the view inline.

`/secure/StructureProcesses.jspa` has title and heading `Manage Effectors`, a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window, and current section `wi-structure-link`. Above the table sit, in a row: text input with placeholder `Effector name`, single-selects with placeholders `Structure` and `Status`, `Run by` for Jira administrators only, and button `Clear all`. Pagination sits below the table. The form never submits.
After the `StructureProcesses` page has started, the query string is removed from the address bar without reloading, so `structureId` pre-selects the filter only on arrival.
Rows per page on `StructureProcesses` are computed once at load: free height is window height minus page height minus 100 px, divided by 35 and rounded down, kept within 10 to 50.

`StructureProcesses` first loads the attribute metadata (see `widget`). Only after it succeeds are filters and table installed; on failure a warning is logged and the page stays without rows or working filters. The page clears the browser's leave-page confirmation, so leaving it never asks.

The table on `StructureProcesses` has columns `ID`, `Effectors`, `Structure`, `Run By`, `Started`, `Finished`, `Status` and `Actions`. Cells of Effectors, Structure, Started, Finished and Status truncate and carry their full text as a tooltip.

Rows of `StructureProcesses` come from `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/list` (the original's URL ends with `/`, which the server treats the same) with JSON body `startAt`, `maxResults` and `params` holding strings `effectorName`, `user`, `status`, `structure`, empty when unset. The page reads `items` and `pagination.total`. The empty, error and loading states are those of the shared paginated table, with texts `No records available` and `Failed to retrieve records from the server`. There is no polling: rows change only on filter, paging or an action.

With a non-blank effector name filter `StructureProcesses` sends `maxResults=-1`, `startAt=0` and empty `effectorName`, caches that full list, keeps entries whose displayed name contains the text, case-insensitively, trimmed, and pages through them in the browser. For a revert process the displayed text matched is `Revert of <id>`; otherwise a process matches when any of its effectors' name does. The total is the filtered count.

On `StructureProcesses` the cached full list is reused while the name filter is non-blank and user, status and structure are unchanged; any other filter change drops it, so the next name search fetches again.

In the `Effector name` input of `StructureProcesses` any key other than Enter schedules a filter update 350 ms after the last key; Enter updates at once and does not submit. Choosing an entry in a select updates at once. An update that leaves all four values unchanged sends nothing; a changed one returns to the first page. Text changed without the keyboard is not noticed until the next key.

The `Structure` filter of `StructureProcesses` is a single-select with a dropdown button that asks `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure` with `filterById=true`, `limit=20` and `name` set to the typed text, or empty when a structure is already selected. It lists the reply's `structures`, each with value `id` and label `<name> (id: <id>)`.

The `Run by` filter of `StructureProcesses` is a single-select that asks Jira's own `GET /rest/api/2/user/picker` with `showAvatar=true` and `maxResults=20`, with the typed text as Jira's select sends it. It lists the reply's `users` by `displayName`, with `avatarUrl` and highlighted `html`, value `key`, and shows the reply's `header` as the group footer.
A filter select of `StructureProcesses` showing text that matches nothing displays `The value is invalid.`; leaving it empty shows no error.
`Clear all` on `StructureProcesses` empties the name input and all selects, sets all filters to empty and removes error messages in the filter row.
The `ID` cell of `StructureProcesses` links to `<context>/secure/StructureEffectorAudit.jspa?processId=<id>`.

The `Effectors` cell of `StructureProcesses`, for a revert process, reads `Revert of <id>` with the id linked to that process's audit page. Otherwise it lists effectors joined by `, `, each linking to `<context>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<structure id>#itemId=com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector/<effector id>`, or plain text for a one-off effector with no id. Names run through the attribute label rule. With no `structure` in the record the cell is empty, also for a run that has a name.

On `StructureProcesses` displayed effector names are cached by effector id for the page's life, and all one-off effectors share the empty id, so every one-off row shows the name of the first one rendered (as the original does).

The `Structure` cell of `StructureProcesses` links the name to `<context>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`, shows `#<id> (deleted)` when the record has no name, and is empty with no structure. `Run By` links `displayName` to the user's `profileUrl` with Jira's user hover (`name`); with no `user` it shows the escaped `userKey`.

The `Status` cell of `StructureProcesses` has the status icon, then `<percentComplete>%` for `CALCULATING` and `IN_PROGRESS`, otherwise the status name: `Pending`, `Calculated`, `Queued`, `Completed`, `Completed with Errors`, `Calculation Stopped`, `Execution Interrupted`, `Execution Stopped`, `Failed`.

`Actions` of a process on `StructureProcesses`, in this order: `Resume` for `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`; `Revert` for `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`, `APPLY_STOPPED`; `Stop` for `PENDING`, `CALCULATING`, `CALCULATED`, `QUEUED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, shown as disabled text when `status.canceled` is true. Other statuses have none.
On `StructureProcesses` no action leaves the cell empty, one action is a plain link, and two or more go in a dropdown opened from a "more" icon with tooltip `Actions`.

Each action on `StructureProcesses` first asks through a confirmation dialog, titled `Confirmation` with `Confirm` and a cancel choice. Confirmed, it sends a JSON POST with body `{}` and the table is in its loading state until the answer. On failure an error flag shows the reply's `localizedMessage`, or `There was an error communicating with the server: <HTTP status>` when the reply is not JSON. Flags close automatically.

`Revert` on `StructureProcesses` asks `Are you sure you want to revert changes made by process #<id>?` and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/undo`. On success a success flag says `Revert process #<new id> successfully created`, with the id linked to its audit page. The table is not refreshed.

`Stop` on `StructureProcesses` asks `Are you sure you want to stop process #<id>?` and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/cancelAndWait`. By `status.status` of the reply: still stoppable gives success flag `Process #<id> has received a stop request and will handle it after some time`; `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `APPLY_STOPPED` gives success flag `Process #<id> was stopped`; anything else gives error flag `Process cannot stop because it has already finished`. In all cases the row is redrawn from the reply.

`Resume` on `StructureProcesses` asks `Are you sure you want to resume applying previously calculated effects?` and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/resume`. On success a success flag says `Process #<id> was successfully resumed`, with the id linked to its audit page, and the row is redrawn from the reply.

Web-resource `effector-audit` depends on `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:page-util` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:dialog-common`. The `StructureEffectorAudit` page requires it and starts the view inline.

`/secure/StructureEffectorAudit.jspa` has title and heading `Effector Process Audit` and a link to the plugin's documentation, opening in a new window. Below: a trail `Manage Effectors` (link to `StructureProcesses.jspa`) ` / ` and the process id in bold; then labelled rows `Effectors`, `Structure` (only with a structure; the link opens in a new tab), `Run by` (Jira's user hover and profile link at `/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=<name>`, new tab), `Started`, `Finished` and `Status` (icon and name).

After the attribute metadata has loaded, effector names in the head of the `StructureEffectorAudit` page show the current label of their attribute, falling back to `Attribute`; a metadata failure only logs a warning and the rest of the page works.

On `StructureEffectorAudit` the Status row of an `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` process has a `Resume` link. It asks `Are you sure you want to resume applying previously calculated effects?` in a confirmation dialog; on Confirm the page sends `GET StructureEffectorAudit!resume.jspa?processId=<id>&atl_token=<token>`, following redirects, and when the answer was redirected replaces the location with the final URL. A failure gives no message.
Rows per page on `StructureEffectorAudit` are computed once at load: free height (window height minus page height) divided by 35, rounded down, minus 1, kept within 8 to 50.

Rows of `StructureEffectorAudit` come from `POST /rest/structure/2.0/effectorProcess/<id>/records` (the original's URL ends with `/`) with JSON `startAt`, `maxResults`, and `params` `{itemKey}` only while a filter is set. Empty, error and loading states are those of the shared paginated table. The page clears the browser's leave-page confirmation.

The table on `StructureEffectorAudit` has columns: a select-all checkbox, `Items`, `Reverse action`, `Effect`, and an unnamed one with the row's `Revert` link. `Items`, `Reverse action` and `Effect` show `affectedItems`, `undo` and `effect` as drawn by the effect renderer, with a missing value marked as such (see `widget-bare`).
A record with `isError` on `StructureEffectorAudit` has no checkbox and no `Revert` link, and its effect text is styled as an error.

The filter on `StructureEffectorAudit` is a text input with placeholder `Enter item key` and button `Filter`; Enter acts as the button and does not submit. A value must match one or more characters, then `-` or `:`, then a number without a leading zero (`ABC-12`, `MEMO:5`); otherwise `Invalid item key format` shows and nothing is sent. Typing hides that message. An empty value removes the filter. A changed value returns to the first page and clears the selection; the same value sends nothing.

On `StructureEffectorAudit` the selection survives paging. The header checkbox acts on the rows of the current page, shows ticked only when all of them are, is hidden when the page has no selectable row, and is disabled while loading. `Revert selected` shows the count and is disabled at 0.
When the record count is known `StructureEffectorAudit` shows `<n> records in total`, and the footer with pagination, total and revert buttons is shown only when the count is above 0.

`Revert all` on `StructureEffectorAudit` is rendered disabled when the process has no successful records. With an item filter set it still reverts all records of the process, not only those shown. It submits `selectedIndexes=null`, read as all.

Any revert on `StructureEffectorAudit` goes through a confirmation dialog `Are you sure you want to revert changes made by process #<id>?`. On Confirm the form posts to `StructureEffectorAudit!undoEffects.jspa` with `atl_token`, `processId` and `selectedIndexes`, a JSON array of record indexes, or `null` for all. A row's `Revert` link submits just that record's index.

On `StructureEffectorAudit`, after a row's `Revert` is cancelled in the dialog, the hidden `selectedIndexes` still holds that row until the selection next changes, so `Revert selected` right after it reverts the cancelled row instead of the checked ones (as the original does).

The `StructureEffectorEdit` dialog has the descriptor's title, the optional description, field `Name` with placeholder `Enter effector name`, the effector's own form, then buttons. Name is marked required only without generated names, is disabled when not configurable, and shows any `effectorName` error. Hidden fields: `atl_token`, `execute=true`, `effectorId`, `structureId`, `moduleKey`, `formAction`. The form posts to `StructureEffectorEdit!apply.jspa`.

With generated names the `StructureEffectorEdit` dialog also shows the summary beside the name field, with edit and clear controls, driven by the effector editor code from the descriptor's summary template with the effector's module key and whether it is configurable (see `widget-bare`).

Buttons of `StructureEffectorEdit`: configurable and executable: `Save and Run`, `Save`; configurable only: `Save`; executable only: `Run`; neither: none. `Cancel` is always there. Clicking one sets `formAction` to `save-and-run`, `save` or `run`.

When `StructureEffectorEdit` is not configurable the page disables every visible input except `Run`, hides the attribute editor's menu, shows plain selects instead of enhanced ones, and focuses `Run` when present.
The error view of `StructureEffectorEdit` is dialog content: the title `Error` and one error box per message.

Every `StructureEffectorProcess` view opens with title `Run Effectors`, row `Effectors` with the effectors title and, for an existing process, row `Status` with icon and name. When the board's widget is present, attribute labels in the title are filled in after the metadata loads; otherwise the title stays as rendered.

The start dialog of `StructureEffectorProcess` shows `Process is ready to start` and `Run time can vary depending on the amount of changes. Press Run if everything is ok.` In the footer: when preview is enabled, a toggle `Preview effects before applying`, on by default, sent as `showPreview=true` only when on; `Run`; and `Cancel`. It sends `atl_token`, `execute=true` and `runParams`.

The preview dialog of `StructureEffectorProcess` shows the effects table with 20 rows per page (see `widget-bare`), the total, and buttons `Apply selected` with a count starting at 0, `Apply all`, `Dismiss` and `Save & Close`, which closes without acting. Hidden fields: `atl_token`, `processId`, `selectedIndexes`, `adjustedParameters`.

The progress dialog of `StructureEffectorProcess` shows a spinner, the status name with a percentage, the remaining time, and buttons `Minimize and continue in background` and `Abort`. Reserved messages: `Failed to retrieve the process state from the server.` with `Trying again after a while...` on the next line, and `Failed to abort the process`. Polling and these states belong to `widget-bare`.

The result dialog of `StructureEffectorProcess` shows the status name, the totals per the page's claims, `View history` opening the audit page in a new tab, and for `CALCULATION_FAILED` the error text. Footer: `Resume` for `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`, posting to `!resume`, and `Acknowledge`, posting to `!acknowledge` with `atl_token`, `processId` and `execute=true`.

The `effector-attribute-to-field` form has, in order: required `Attribute` (text area `attributeJson`, with the attribute editor attached), required `Field` (select `fieldId` of supported fields by translated name), required `Action` (select `collectionOperation`: `set` `Set`, `add` `Add`, `remove` `Remove`), `Limit To` (JQL input `jql`, placeholder `Enter JQL to apply the effector only to matching issues in the structure`), and checkbox `sendNotifications` `Send email notifications`. `attributeJson` errors show under their field.
On the `effector-attribute-to-field` form `Action` shows only for a multi-value field. Choosing a single-value field hides it and forces `set`.

On the `effector-attribute-to-field` form `Values of the selected attribute cannot be stored in the chosen field` shows live under `Field` when metadata has loaded, the attribute text is non-empty, is not `{}` and parses as JSON, the field has a required format, and the attribute does not support that format.
Clicking any submit button of the `effector-attribute-to-field` form does nothing while attribute metadata has not loaded or the inconsistency message is showing.

The summary of `effector-attribute-to-field` reads, by `collectionOperation`: `Set <attribute> to issue field <field>`, `Add <attribute> to issue field <field>`, `Remove <attribute> from issue field <field>`. It carries the attribute spec so the browser can show the attribute's current label. In the edit dialog it is the live summary text instead.

The `effector-status-rollup` form has, in order: `Projects` (multi-select `projects`) with toggle `All projects`; `Issue types` (`issueTypes`) with toggle `All types`; `Resolution` (first option, empty, `Use current or default value`, then Jira's resolutions by translated name); checkbox `sendNotifications` `Send email notifications`; the hint `Set statuses based on the following order (earliest to latest):` with link `More about statuses...` to Jira's `ShowConstantsHelp.jspa?decorator=popup#StatusTypes`; the ordered statuses; and, only when configurable, a status select with `Clear all`. Behaviour of these controls belongs to `widget-bare`.

The `effector-status-rollup` form shows server errors for `projects`, `issueTypes` and `resolution` under their fields; the status field's slot looks for a misspelt key (`stasuses`), so a server error under `statuses` is not displayed there (as the original does).
In the `effector-status-rollup` form the drag handle and delete control of a status appear on hover, and never when the form is not configurable.
The summary of `effector-status-rollup` reads `Roll up status: <status names>`; in the edit dialog it is the live summary text instead.
The `effector-delay` form has text inputs `Preview delay` (`previewDelay`) and `Apply delay` (`applyDelay`), each followed by `ms`. Its summary reads `Delay: preview <n>ms, apply <m>ms`.
The `effector-conversion` form has one checkbox, `skipItemReplace`: `Create tickets in Jira without replacing planning tasks in structure`. Its summary reads `Convert Planning Task to Issue`.
Mail `shared-perspective`, sent as in `perspective-mail-sender`, has subject `<page title> perspective has been shared with you`.

HTML body of `shared-perspective`: the header, then `<page title> perspective has been shared with you`, the title bold when `highlightTitle` is set; a box with the sender's avatar and bold name and below it the HTML-escaped message; a button `View the structure` to `<baseUrl>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?p=<perspective id>`; the footer. With no actor the name is `Anonymous` and there is no avatar image.

Text body of `shared-perspective`: `<page title> perspective has been shared with you by <actor or Anonymous>`, a dashed line, the message, a dashed line, `Link: <baseUrl>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?p=<perspective id>`, an empty line, the footer.

The HTML body of `shared-perspective` uses Jira's standard mail head with a row for the plugin's own logo (the implementer's; not the vendor's) and a footer stating the plugin and its version. The text footer is `--` and the same statement. Vendor links and addresses of the original footers are not part of the replacement. `sync-cycle` and `sync-error` use Jira's own mail head and foot instead.

Mail `sync-cycle`, sent as in `sync-manager`, has subject `Action Required: <product> Synchronizers Confict`, the misspelling included (as the original does), then `, Synchronizers Disabled` when the instances were stopped, then ` (Structure: <name abbreviated to 40 characters>)` when both instances are on one structure.

Body of `sync-cycle`, in both formats, in order: `Hello,`; a sentence that the cycle guard (linked to the plugin's documentation in HTML) found a possible conflict between two or more synchronizers, naming the structure when they share one, that would cause cyclical changes; when stopped, that they were disabled automatically and should be reviewed before re-enabling; otherwise that they were stopped but remain enabled, may cycle again after a user change, and should be fixed soon to avoid overloading Jira; then `Synchronizers Configuration:`, `Number of executions of each synchronizer detected: <n>`, the action section, `We apologize for the inconvenience.`, the reason for receiving it, a pointer to the plugin's documentation and support, and the sign-off `Sincerely Yours,` with the plugin's name.

The configuration part of `sync-cycle`: when structures differ, `First structure:` and `Second structure:` with the name and `<baseUrl>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>`; then `First synchronizer (ID=<id>):` in HTML, `First synchronizer: (ID=<id>)` in text, with the description and each detail line, likewise for `Second`. In HTML names are abbreviated to 40 characters and escaped and link to the board; in text names are in full, except in the opening sentence, and lines start with ` * `.

The action section of `sync-cycle` is headed `Action Required:` in HTML, `ACTION REQUIRED` underlined by dashes in text. With one structure it says to use the `Sync Settings page` and gives `<baseUrl>/secure/StructureSync.jspa?id=<id>`; with two, the `Sync Settings pages` and both URLs. The text format with one structure also starts with that URL in brackets, indented, before `Hello,`.

The reason in `sync-cycle`, with `owners` true: `You are receiving this email because at least one of the synchronizers runs under your account.` With `owners` false: `You are receiving this email because you are the administrator of this JIRA instance.` and a sentence that the cycle guard's settings can be changed as documented.
Mail `sync-error`, sent as in `sync-manager`, has subject `Action Required: <product> Synchronizer Needs Attention (Structure: <name abbreviated to 40 characters>)`.

Body of `sync-error`, both formats, in order: `Hello,`; `A <product> synchronizer that you've installed needs your attention.`; `Structure:` with the name and board link (HTML: abbreviated to 40 characters, linked; text: in full, then the URL); the synchronizer with `(ID=<id>)`, description and detail lines; `The following problems were reported:` with each error message after `* `; the action section with `<baseUrl>/secure/StructureSync.jspa?id=<id>`; `We apologize for the inconvenience.`; `You are receiving this email because the synchronizer runs under your account.`; a pointer to the plugin's support; and the sign-off. The text format starts with the settings URL in brackets, indented.
